spans.s:
Kabandha Ātharvaṇa is mentioned in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka
Upaniṣad^1 along with Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa, as a teacher, but
is semi-mythical. His son was Vicārin

) vi. 7, 1. Cf. also Gopatha Brāh-
maṇa, i. 2, 9. 18; Hillebrandt, Vedische
Mythologie, 2, 176, n. 4; Weber, Indian
Literature, 149.

Kābandhi (‘descendant of Kabandha’) is the patronymic of
Vicārin in the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa (i. 2, 9. 18).
